approach: Add one reading-gate check, `check_speed_timeline(reading, request)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, wired as one `step!(check_speed_timeline(reading, request));` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_outcome_state`. Root cause named everywhere: the reading stage checked a request's own figures only if the reader chose to, so readings were planned around stated timings with no stage timeline from the code; the fix sits at the reading gate every speed request passes. A request is a speed request in three ways. (1) Structural: a line starts with Hestia's own `SLOWDOWN_MARKER` or `THROUGHPUT_MARKER` (hestia.rs:1304/1314), the two speed requests Athena writes itself. (2) Stand-alone cues over whole words from `request_words`: faster, quicker, speedup, latency, `speed up`, `head start`, and 'take/takes/took longer' or 'take too long'. (3) Phrase cues: a cut verb whose object is a duration, or whose duration follows `by`/`off`; a duration after `to` when a cut verb and a time noun come first; a duration after `under`/`below`/`within` when a time noun comes first; a narrow shorten verb followed by a time noun; and slow*/delay*/timing* only after a cut verb or `too`. Setting words (timeout, interval, ttl, retry, backoff …) cancel a phrase cue. For a root-cause request (a line starts with the shared `ROOT_CAUSE_MARKER`), only the `Introspection … ; prevention it proposed:` lines are dropped before scanning, because they quote proposed rules; the Cause and Failure class lines are scanned, so a repeated cause that is itself slowness is still a speed request. For a speed request the reading needs a `Timeline:` assumption naming a crates/ path, a `stages:` list of at least two stages each with a duration (unless it says no recorded timing), and a place word followed by a stage name. The fake reader gets one fixed Timeline so the drain test at drain.rs:7008 passes the real gate, and a drain test pins it against both the speed gate and `check_reading_references`.

decisions.choice: Enforce at the reading gate: one `step!` in `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3226), placed after `check_outcome_state`.
decisions.reason: Every reading passes `refusing_check`; the corpus test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case per step; no model call is needed; a refused reading gets one re-read with the refusal text. `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` needs `check_outcome_state` right after `check_governance_coverage`; a step after it leaves that position alone.

rejected.option: Prompt-only guidance (reader brief or reader.md)
rejected.why: Prose only; the reader can ignore it, which is the failure. The 'mechanism' default requires a check; reader.md and the planner/critic prompts are out of scope.

rejected.option: A planner-stage check (plan_findings)
rejected.why: By then the reading is accepted and the criteria are fixed around the request's figure.

rejected.option: A verifier-stage check
rejected.why: Runs after the producer built the wrong thing; the failure is in planning.

rejected.option: Have Athena run the stages at reading time
rejected.why: A build and test run per reading; unbounded cost; beyond one producer run.

decisions.choice: Answers critic finding 4. Treat Hestia's two own speed requests as structural speed signals: `speed_request` is true when any line of the request starts with `crate::hestia::SLOWDOWN_MARKER` or `crate::hestia::THROUGHPUT_MARKER`. Add the human forms the critic named: 'takes longer' and 'takes too long' (a take-form word then `longer`, or `too long`), 'get the checks under 6 minutes' (a duration after under/below/within with a time noun before it), 'reduce CI time to 6 minutes' (a duration after `to` with a cut verb and a time noun before it), and 'shorten the run/stage/wait' (a shorten verb, then a time noun within three words). Pin each with a corpus positive and with hestia.rs tests that pass the real `slowdown_request` and `throughput_request` output through `speed_request`.
decisions.reason: `slowdown_request` (hestia.rs:1735) renders 'takes longer', 'shortens that stage' and a measured stage median, and `throughput_request` (hestia.rs:1611) is built around 'Predicted saving: N minutes', which is the failure class: planning around a predicted timing figure. Word cues alone would see neither unless a model's text happened to hold 'faster'. The markers are `pub const` already and used by `open_request_with_marker` (hestia.rs:1651), so sharing them cannot drift. The Timeline is natural for both: the slowdown request names the stage and its measured medians, and the design request names a Stage line. Time-noun lists are two: a wide one (time, duration, runtime, run, runs, build, builds, check, checks, test, tests, suite, pipeline, ci, stage, stages, compile, wait) for the figure-target rules, and a narrow one (time, duration, runtime, run, runs, stage, stages, wait, pipeline) for the shorten rule so 'shorten the error message' and 'save the test results' are not cues.

rejected.option: Leave Hestia's requests to word cues
rejected.why: 'takes longer' and 'shortens that stage' are not cues, so the slowdown request would pass unseen; the throughput design request would pass unless its model-written text had a cue.

rejected.option: Treat `too long` alone as a cue
rejected.why: 'the title is too long' is not about speed; only the take-form phrase is used.

rejected.option: One wide time-noun list for shorten
rejected.why: 'Shorten the test names' or 'save the test results' would be flagged.

rejected.option: Exempt the throughput design request because it only edits docs/design/
rejected.why: It is planned around a predicted minutes figure, the class this change prevents; the reader can name a crates/ path and stages from THROUGHPUT.md.

decisions.choice: Answers critic finding 5. Quoted-record handling drops only the `Introspection … ; prevention it proposed:` lines, and only when the request is a root-cause request (some line starts with `ROOT_CAUSE_MARKER`, 'Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: '). The title, `Failure class:` and `Cause:` lines are scanned. The three prefixes are `pub const` in hestia.rs (`ROOT_CAUSE_MARKER`, `INTROSPECTION_PREFIX`, `PREVENTION_MARK`), next to the other markers, and `root_cause_request_at` (hestia.rs:458-507) formats with them so the rendered bytes stay identical; reading.rs imports them.
decisions.reason: The prevention lines quote other jobs' proposed rules (this job's own request quotes 'claims a delay or speed-up'), so they describe a rule to change and are not this job's goal; scanning them would refuse a request with no truthful Timeline. The Cause line is the request's substance: a repeated cause such as 'verifier runs time out because the suite is too slow' is a speed fix and must pass the gate. The strict phrase rules keep this job's own visible Cause ('a timing figure', 'real stage order and durations', 'the class already exists for a speed') from being a cue: 'timing' has no cut verb or `too` before it, and `speed` is not followed by `up`. A hestia.rs test pins the text of this job's own cause as not a speed request. A request that is not root-cause-shaped is scanned whole, so a person's own 'Cause: it is slow, make it faster' is seen.

rejected.option: Drop Cause, Failure class and Introspection lines (previous plan)
rejected.why: Exempts a root-cause request whose repeated cause is slowness (critic finding 5).

rejected.option: Scan the whole request including prevention text
rejected.why: False positive on every root-cause request that quotes a speed-related prevention, including this job's own.

rejected.option: Duplicate the prefix strings in reading.rs
rejected.why: They drift from hestia.rs; one set of consts used by both is safer.

rejected.option: Skip any line starting with 'Cause:' in every request
rejected.why: Hides cues in a person's own request that happens to use the word.

decisions.choice: A cut verb (cut, cuts, save, saves, reduce, reduces, shave, shaves, trim, trims, lower, lowers) is a strong cue only when a duration figure (a number glued to or followed by s, ms, sec, second(s), min, minute(s), or h/hour(s)) is its object (the figure starts within two words after the verb, optionally after about, around, another, roughly, nearly, almost) or follows `by`/`off` within five words after the verb, with no setting word between. Setting words: timeout(s), interval(s), ttl, expiry, retention, lifetime, retry, backoff, debounce. Weak words (slow, slower, slowest, slowly, slowdown, delay, delays, delayed, timing, timings) count only with a cut verb within five words before them and no setting word between, or with `too` right before.
decisions.reason: Keeps settings changes out: 'Save the state every 30 seconds', 'Reduce the retry timeout to 10 s', 'Trim the log after 5 minutes', 'Set the retry timeout to 10 s', 'Add a retry delay setting' and 'Fix a timing attack' are not speed requests, while 'Save 12 minutes', 'Cut 5 minutes from the checks', 'Reduce the check time by 5 minutes' and 'Shave 30 s off the run' are. Whole-word cues over `request_words` (reading.rs:3503, splits bullets, `1.`, `2)`, `(a)` and hyphens) keep slowloris, speedometer, quickstart and timeline out.

rejected.option: Any cut verb with a figure within five words
rejected.why: Flags settings changes such as 'Save the state every 30 seconds'.

rejected.option: Bare delay, timing or slow as cues
rejected.why: Common in requests that are not about speed.

rejected.option: Substring match like the fake reader's SPEED_WORDS
rejected.why: Matches inside other words and drifts from the gate.

decisions.choice: The Timeline must hold a crates/ path (`names_crates_path`, reading.rs:3838), a `stages:` clause with at least two ordered stages, a duration per stage (unless the Timeline says 'no recorded timing'), and a clause with a place word (sits, slowest, longest, bottleneck) followed by one of the stage names. 'No recorded timing' replaces only the durations, never the stages or the place. The gate checks the shape of the Timeline, not whether its figures are true; the doc comment and D163 say so.
decisions.reason: The three introspections ask for each stage in order, its measured duration and where the claimed delay sits. Stage order and place can be read from the code; only durations may be missing from records. A text-only gate cannot verify figures.

rejected.option: A stock 'no recorded timing' phrase plus a crates/ path clears the check
rejected.why: One fixed sentence would clear every speed request without the stage order, which is the cause.

rejected.option: Keep 'delay' as a place word
rejected.why: 'the claimed delay is real' would pass without placing the delay in a stage.

rejected.option: Check only when the request holds a duration figure
rejected.why: The class includes 'make it faster' with no figure.

decisions.choice: Keep the crates/ path requirement and state the limit in D163: a target repository with no crates/ directory cannot meet the rule.
decisions.reason: It mirrors `check_code_survey` and the reading's contract (the Timeline names the crates/ code read). Athena's own repository is the target today; a non-crates generalisation is a named follow-up.

rejected.option: Accept any slash path the reading references
rejected.why: Widens the rule beyond the reading's contract; `check_reading_references` checks existence only for known top directories.

risks.risk: False refusals: a request that uses a cut verb plus `by`/`off`/`to` and a figure for a non-speed purpose is refused until the reader writes a Timeline (for example 'Reduce the grace period by 5 minutes' is a cue by the `by` rule).
risks.mitigation: Setting words (timeout, interval, ttl, retry, backoff …), the object-of-verb rule, and the time-noun requirement for the `to`/`under` forms keep the common settings forms out, pinned by accept cases. The reader gets one re-read with refusal text saying what to write, and can use the no-recorded-timing form. The declared 5% is an estimate, not measured.

demonstrations.method: Run the refusal corpus. New cases in `speed_timeline_cases()` give a speed request and a reading with no Timeline and expect `Expected::Refuse("check_speed_timeline")`. Case ids by input form: 'speed-request-without-a-timeline' ('Move the call earlier to save 12 minutes.'); dash bullet `speed-word-in-a-dash-bullet`; star bullet `speed-word-in-a-star-bullet`; `1.` part `speed-word-in-a-numbered-dot-part`; `2)` part `speed-word-in-a-numbered-paren-part`; `(a)` part `speed-word-in-a-lettered-paren-part`; retry complaint `retry-complaint-still-too-slow-without-a-timeline` (accept twin `…-with-a-timeline`); a request that cites a job without relying on it: the existing `root-cause-request-cites-jobs…` cases at refusal_corpus.rs:604-617 stay Accept, and new `root-cause-request-with-its-own-speed-goal-without-a-timeline` (Refuse, own line 'Make the check faster.'); `root-cause-request-whose-cause-is-slowness-without-a-timeline` (Refuse; Hestia-shaped Cause 'verifier runs time out because the suite is too slow'); Hestia's own requests `slowdown-request-without-a-timeline` (Refuse, text from the same shape as `slowdown_request`) and `throughput-design-request-without-a-timeline` (Refuse); human forms `takes-too-long-without-a-timeline`, `get-the-checks-under-6-minutes-without-a-timeline`, `reduce-ci-time-to-6-minutes-without-a-timeline`, `shorten-the-run-without-a-timeline` (all Refuse); crate-relative path `timeline-with-a-crate-relative-path` (Refuse, names src/reading.rs); a brand word or environment variable is not read by this rule, so no case is added. Timeline-defect Refuse cases: `timeline-without-a-crates-path`, `timeline-with-one-stage-only`, `timeline-stage-without-a-duration`, `timeline-says-no-recorded-timing-without-stages`, `timeline-without-where-the-delay-sits`, `timeline-place-word-names-no-stage`, `timeline-label-not-at-the-start`. Each is built from `base_reading()` with one field changed so no earlier check refuses. Run: `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. Observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` passes, so each Refuse case is refused by `check_speed_timeline` and by no earlier check; `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` passes with the new step in the extracted list; `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` passes with the new tags.
demonstrations.observes: All Refuse cases are refused by check_speed_timeline; every step has a refusing case; the input-form tag list is covered.

Drop the structural marker rule and the slowdown and throughput cases fail. Drop the 'takes longer' and target-figure cues and the human-form cases fail. demonstrations.method: The same corpus run holds accept cases, and unit tests call the detector and check directly. Corpus accepts: 'speed-request-with-a-timeline' (assumption 'Timeline: read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs; stages: compile 9 min, check 40 s; the delay sits in compile.'); 'speed-request-timeline-says-no-recorded-timing' (stages named, no durations, place given); retry, root-cause-shaped, slowdown-request and throughput-design requests each with a Timeline; 'root-cause-request-quoting-speed-words-in-its-prevention-needs-no-timeline' (Hestia-shaped: Cause without a cue; the Introspection prevention lines hold 'speed-up', 'faster', 'cut 5 minutes'); 'speed-request-question-reading-needs-no-timeline'; 'speed-word-lookalikes-are-not-speed-requests' ('Add a timeline view and a speedometer widget. Write a quickstart guide. Wait 30 seconds before the retry. Cover the slowloris case.'); non-speed pins 'add-a-retry-delay-setting-…', 'fix-a-timing-attack-…', 'save-the-state-every-30-seconds-…', 'set-the-retry-timeout-to-10-s-…', 'reduce-the-retry-timeout-by-5-s-…', 'trim-the-log-after-5-minutes-…', 'reduce-the-grace-period-to-5-minutes-…', 'the-title-is-too-long-…', 'shorten-the-error-message-…' (each ending `-is-not-a-speed-request`), and the existing `steward-three-dash-bullets`. reading.rs unit tests `speed_requests_are_found_by_whole_word_cues_and_figures` and `a_timeline_assumption_needs_stages_durations_and_a_placed_delay` cover positives ('Make the check faster', 'Speed up planning', 'a speed-up of the run', 'Cut 5 minutes from the checks', 'Save 12 minutes', 'Shave 30 s off the run', 'reduce the delay', 'still too slow', 'It takes longer now', 'Get the checks under 6 minutes', 'Reduce CI time to 6 minutes', 'Shorten the run'), the negatives above, and the Timeline defects (accept; no label; label not at the start; no crates/ path; crate-relative path; one stage; stage without a duration; no-recorded-timing without stages refused; with stages and place accepted; no place word; place word with no stage after it; 'delay' alone not placing; question and decline skip; one-line error starting 'the reading was refused because'). hestia.rs tests (step 5) feed real builder output through `crate::reading::speed_request`: `slowdown_request(25.0, 60.0, &growth)` (the form used at hestia.rs:5765) expects true; `throughput_request` with a `ThroughputOutput` expects true; `root_cause_request` with prevention text holding speed words and a Cause with no cue expects false; the same with a Cause 'verifier runs time out because the suite is too slow' expects true; this job's own visible Cause text ('…a timing figure… real stage order and durations… The class already exists for a speed…') expects false; the cue-free root-cause text plus an own line 'Make it faster.' expects true. Run: `cargo test -p athena-core`.
demonstrations.observes: All accept cases return None from refusing_check; unit and hestia tests pass; the one-line errors start 'the reading was refused because'; the no-timing escape needs stages and place; the check is skipped when capability is None or a question is set.
